messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: KV-cache eviction spike detected in us-east1-pool. Severity: P1. Paging primary oncall @Aisha. Auto-escalation: 2m.
Aisha: Ack. I'm checking eviction rates + recent deploys. Starting with Grafana -> kv-cache dashboard.
Marco: I'm seeing eviction_count jump ~x6 around 03:17 UTC. Hit rate drops from 92% -> 53%. Pools affected: shared-read, lowmem-burst.
Aisha: Any deploys around that time? /deploybot logs?
Marco: No deploys logged for that service in the last 6 hours. But autoscaler added 3 pods to shared-read pool at 03:15.
Priya: Could be eviction policy + new pod mem pressure. Looking at pod logs now.
Tomas: Logged these queries on the cache node: 
```
sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m])) by (pool)
avg_over_time(kv_cache_hit_ratio[5m])
sum(rate(kv_cache_set_memory_pressure_bytes[1m])) by (pool)
```
Carla: Confirming eviction spike correlates with a pull-heavy traffic burst from a single customer (acct: acct-942). Trying to throttle their requests at the routing layer.
Aisha: Mitigation plan: 1) Apply temporary rate limit to acct-942 (done) 2) Increase cache_max_entries for shared-read pool by 20% as emergency (rolling) 3) If eviction continues, pin a larger instance to that pool. Executing step 1 now.
Marco: Rate limit applied. Eviction rate dropped ~40% in the last 90s. Hit rate back to ~78% but still below baseline.
incident-bot: NOTE: Customer-facing errors: 4.8% increase in 5xx for API key group: low-tier, tail latency +300ms.
Aisha: Noted. Notify support to flag any customer escalations. Carla please open an incident ticket with affected accounts.
Carla: Created INC-2026-0472 and added affected accounts, latency graphs, and current mitigation notes. Link: https://redwood.inc/INC-2026-0472
Priya: Running post-mortem checks on eviction policy. There's a race in our LRU compactor under memory pressure that can cause mass-evictions when many small keys churn.
Tomas: I can push a quick fix: reduce compactor aggressive_threshold from 0.9 -> 0.75 to smooth eviction behavior. I'll roll a config change to one canary node first.
Aisha: OK canary it, watch hit-rate and latency. If green, roll to pool.
Tomas: Canary applied to us-east1-canary-01. Watching.
Marco: Canary looks stable after 4m. Evictions per min down to normal. Hit rate trending back to 89%.
Aisha: Good. I'm going to start handoff in 30m. Priya, can you take the long investigation and postmortem? Make sure we capture monitoring/action items.
Priya: Taking handoff. /incident handoff to @Priya
incident-bot: Handoff noted: Aisha -> Priya at 1999009000.
Aisha: Thanks team. Quick notes for the oncall follow-up: we reduced false pages by throttling a noisy customer; we applied a temporary <20% cache size bump; canaried compactor config that fixed mass-evictions.
Carla: Support notified customers in the affected cohort. No escalations so far. :thumbsup:
---
Priya (post-incident, follow-up): Drafting monitoring and alert tuning changes to prevent noisy pages and improve signal-to-noise.
Priya: Proposed alert logic (Prometheus pseudo):
```
alert: KVCacheEvictionSpike
expr: sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])) by (pool) > 50
for: 5m
labels: {severity="warning"}
annotations: {summary="Eviction spike", runbook="https://redwood.runbooks/kv-cache-eviction"}
```
Priya: But paging threshold should be stricter and require hit-rate degradation or impact on latency. New paging rule proposal:
```
page when (eviction_rate > 200/min total) OR (eviction_rate > 50/min AND kv_cache_hit_ratio_drop > 20% for 5m)
```
Priya: Also propose: 1) Add a Grafana panel for per-pool eviction_rate and hit_ratio, 2) Add a "squelch" window for non-customer-facing high-frequency transient spikes (auto-squelch 3m if no latency impact), 3) Group alerts by pool and include top-3 affected accounts in annotation.
Tomas: I'll add the Grafana panel under infra -> kv-cache and include the PromQL queries and an alerting template.
Carla: I'll add a support playbook snippet for telling customers what happened and the mitigation steps.
Marco: Also suggest adding low-priority metric to routing to throttle top offenders automatically when their request rate > X qps per minute to avoid paging.
Priya: Creating Jira: RED-3612 "Alert tuning + dashboards for KV cache evictions" and linking INC-2026-0472. Assigning to Tomas for dashboards, Marco for routing change, Carla for support message, Aisha for rollout guidance.
incident-bot: Ticket created RED-3612.
Priya: Postmortem will include timeline, root cause (compactor threshold + customer churn), impact (latency increase ~300ms tail, 4.8% error bump), mitigations, and follow-ups above.
Aisha: One more ops note: update runbook to include immediate mitigations: rate-limit top offender, canary compactor config, temporarily increase cache_max_entries, and escalate to infra if we need to pin capacity.
Priya: Will do. Closing the live paging — switching to monitoring-only. Please triage anything else into RED-3612. :eyes:
Carla: Marking incident as Resolved (mitigated) in INC-2026-0472. Last checks show stable hit rate and latency within 10% of baseline.
Marco: Adding grafana snapshots to ticket.
Tomas: Will follow up with a config PR for compactor default change and add a safety throttle to the compactor.
Aisha: Thanks everyone. Great coordination. :heart:
